vigtig.explanation: "Vigtig" means "important". To say who something matters to, add "for" (for): "Det er vigtigt for mig" (It is important to me). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et vigtigt møde" (an important meeting).

vikingetiden.explanation: "Vikingetiden" means "the Viking Age". It is built from "viking" (Viking) and "tiden" (the time). In Danish history, it is dated from about 800 to 1050. To say something happened then: "Skibene blev bygget i vikingetiden" (The ships were built in the Viking Age).

vild.explanation: "Vild" means "wild", as in an animal or plant that lives free. To talk about plants that grow free: "vilde blomster" (wild flowers). A different use: to say a party was amazing, say "Den fest var vild" (That party was amazing).

vild med.explanation: "Vild med" means "crazy about". It comes after "er" (am/is/are): "Jeg er vild med pizza" (I am crazy about pizza). When more than one person feels it, "vild" becomes "vilde": "De er vilde med sne" (They are crazy about snow).

vildt.explanation: "Vildt" means "wild". It is the form of "vild" (wild) used in front of a word that takes "et": "et vildt dyr" (a wild animal). A different use: to react to something amazing, say "Det var vildt!" (That was crazy!)

villig.explanation: "Villig" means "willing". To say what someone is willing to do, add "til at" (to) before the verb: "Hun er villig til at hjælpe" (She is willing to help). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et villigt barn" (a willing child).

villighed.explanation: "Villighed" means "willingness". It is built from "villig" (willing). To thank someone for being ready to help: "Tak for din villighed" (Thank you for your willingness).

vind.explanation: "Vind" means "wind". To say it is windy, use "at blæse" (to blow): "Det blæser i dag" (It is windy today).

vindende.explanation: "Vindende" means "winning". It comes from "at vinde" (to win). A different use: a smile that charms people is "et vindende smil" (a winning smile).

vindenergi.explanation: "Vindenergi" means "wind power". It is built from "vind" (wind) and "energi" (energy). To say a country makes wind power: "Danmark producerer meget vindenergi" (Denmark produces a lot of wind power).

vinterbadning.explanation: "Vinterbadning" means "winter swimming". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "badning" (bathing), from "at bade" (to bathe). In Denmark, many people swim in the sea in winter and meet in a club. To say you do it: "Jeg går til vinterbadning hver søndag" (I go winter swimming every Sunday).

viral.explanation: "Viral" means "viral". To say a post spread fast online: "Opslaget blev viralt" (The post went viral). A different use: to say a disease is caused by a virus: "en viral infektion" (a viral infection).

virkelig.explanation: "Virkelig" means "really". To make a word stronger: "virkelig dejlig" (really lovely). To react to surprising news: "Virkelig?" (Really?)

visdom.explanation: "Visdom" means "wisdom". It is the first part of "en visdomstand" (a wisdom tooth) and "et visdomsord" (a word of wisdom).

visse.explanation: "Visse" means "certain". To talk about one certain thing, use "en vis" or "et vist": "en vis tid" (a certain time). To say you are sure, use "sikker" (sure): "Jeg er sikker" (I am sure).

vist.explanation: "Vist" means "I think". To say you believe something but are not sure, put it after the verb: "Han er vist syg" (I think he is sick). A different use: "vist" is also the word for "shown", as in "Filmen blev vist i går" (The film was shown yesterday).

vistnok.explanation: "Vistnok" means "I believe". It is built from "vist" (I think) and "nok" (probably). To pass on something you heard but are not sure of: "Hun er vistnok hjemme" (She is home, I believe).

vittig.explanation: "Vittig" means "witty". A joke is "en vittighed": "Han fortæller en vittighed" (He tells a joke). Do not mix it up with "vigtig" (important): "Det er vigtigt" (It is important).

voksen.explanation: "Voksen" means "grown-up". It comes from "at vokse" (to grow). As a noun, "en voksen" is a grown-up: "børn og voksne" (children and grown-ups).

vold.explanation: "Vold" means "violence". To say someone uses violence: "at bruge vold" (to use violence). To say it is forbidden: "Vold i hjemmet er forbudt" (Violence in the home is forbidden).

voldelig.explanation: "Voldelig" means "violent", as in hurting people. It is built from "vold" (violence). For a storm or a pain with great force, use "voldsom" (violent): "en voldsom storm" (a violent storm).

voldsom.explanation: "Voldsom" means "violent", as in great force. It is built from "vold" (violence). To describe a person who hurts others, use "voldelig" (violent): "Han er voldelig" (He is violent).

volleyball.explanation: "Volleyball" means "volleyball". To say you play it, use "at spille" (to play): "Hun spiller volleyball hver tirsdag" (She plays volleyball every Tuesday). It starts longer words: "en volleyballkamp" (a volleyball match).

vores.explanation: "Vores" means "our". It does not change, whatever follows: "vores børn" (our children).

vred.explanation: "Vred" means "angry". To name who you are angry at, use "på" (at): "Jeg er vred på dig" (I am angry at you). When more than one person is angry, "vred" becomes "vrede": "De er vrede på mig" (They are angry at me).
